skill.name: ubiquitous-language
skill.description: Extract a DDD-style ubiquitous language glossary from the current conversation, flagging ambiguities and proposing canonical terms. Saves to UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md. Use when user wants to define domain terms, build a glossary, harden terminology, create a ubiquitous language, or mentions "domain model" or "DDD".
skill.summary: Creates a DDD-style glossary from conversation context and saves it as Markdown.
skill.author: mattpocock

content.value_statement: Teams lose clarity when the same domain words mean different things. This skill turns conversation context into a clear DDD glossary.
actual_capabilities: Scans the current conversation for domain nouns, verbs, and concepts.
Identifies synonyms, overloaded words, and ambiguous terms.
Proposes canonical term choices with aliases to avoid.
Writes UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md in a Markdown glossary format.
Adds relationships, flagged ambiguities, and example dialogue.
Updates an existing glossary when run again in the same conversation.
limitations: Uses only the current conversation and existing UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md.
Cannot verify domain truth without user or expert feedback.
May omit important terms that were not discussed.
Produces Markdown guidance, not a formal ontology or schema.

use_cases.title: Align Product Terminology
use_cases.description: Create a shared glossary after a planning discussion so teams use consistent domain terms.

use_cases.title: Clarify Domain Models
use_cases.description: Extract canonical terms and relationships from discovery notes before designing a bounded context.

use_cases.title: Improve Technical Documentation
use_cases.description: Turn implementation discussions into a readable language guide for engineers and stakeholders.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Glossary
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after a short product or domain discussion.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a ubiquitous language glossary from this conversation. Save it to UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md and summarize the key terms.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve Ambiguous Terms
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a team uses several names for related concepts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review our conversation for ambiguous or overloaded domain terms. Choose canonical names and list aliases to avoid.

prompt_templates.title: Model Relationships
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before designing entities, workflows, or bounded contexts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a DDD glossary with grouped terms, relationships, and cardinality where obvious. Highlight terms that need domain expert review.

prompt_templates.title: Refresh Existing Glossary
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after new discussion changes the team language.
prompt_templates.prompt: Read the existing UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md, incorporate the latest conversation, update definitions, and rewrite the example dialogue.

output_examples.input: A checkout team discusses carts, orders, invoices, payments, and account confusion.
output_examples.output: A Markdown glossary with canonical terms, aliases to avoid, relationships, and flagged ambiguity around account.

output_examples.input: A platform team debates sandbox, filesystem layer, Docker layer, sync service, and bundle.
output_examples.output: A grouped domain language guide that separates service names, layers, artifacts, and their relationships.

output_examples.input: A support workflow discussion uses ticket, case, request, customer, and requester inconsistently.
output_examples.output: A terminology guide that recommends one term per concept and explains why confusing aliases should be avoided.

best_practices: Provide real domain discussion before running the skill.
Review flagged ambiguities with a domain expert.
Re-run the skill after major terminology decisions change.
anti_patterns: Using it on conversations with little domain context.
Treating suggested terms as final without expert review.
Including generic programming terms unless they have domain meaning.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md with canonical domain terms, definitions, aliases, relationships, ambiguities, and example dialogue.

faq.question: Does it need an existing glossary?
faq.answer: No. It can create a new glossary or update an existing UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md file.

faq.question: Can it replace domain expert review?
faq.answer: No. It proposes terminology from the conversation, but experts should confirm important definitions.

faq.question: What inputs work best?
faq.answer: Planning notes, discovery discussions, support workflows, product conversations, and architecture debates work well.

faq.question: Does it generate code?
faq.answer: No. It generates Markdown documentation focused on domain language and relationships.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
